title: Pilot Ops: Engineer Quickcards - mini deck (WIP)
audience: Sales engineers, platform engineers, customer success on pilot engagements
objective: Provide a compact, engineering-forward playset for rapid pilot qualification, on-call fallback choreography, and cost/latency tradeoff talking points to keep pilots healthy and convertible.
slide_headlines: 1) Why pilots fail fast: common engineering causes
4) SLA stitching: how to map Redwood's runtime guarantees to customer expectations
5) Quick econ metrics to defuse 'cost shock' objections
6) Live demo scripts & guardrails for SEs
8) Pilot exit criteria and convert signals
speaker_notes: Slide 1: Frame pilots as experiments — remind customers that latency spikes, token budget surprises, and dataset-specific hallucinations are typical. Emphasize how Redwood isolates and mitigates each vector so pilot results are actionable.

Slide 2: 15-min triage: (a) confirm model/variant, (b) reproduce with cURL to rule out SDK, (c) capture request id + sample token counts, (d) switch to cached/quantized variant if cost/latency spike. Keep doc link to SDK debug flags handy.

Slide 3: Fallback choreography: recommended order = same-API smaller-variant -> regional fallback -> degraded quality mode (compression/shorten prompts) -> circuit-breaker to stub response. Map triggers: latency > 2x SLO, token cost > 3x baseline, error rate > 1.5%.

Slide 4: SLA stitching: Translate Redwood latency and availability SLOs into customer-facing statements (“95th p50 pipeline latency under Xms under reserved capacity”). Outline what we can commit in pilot vs. Dedicated.

Slide 5: Quick econ: show simple calc lines (tokens per user * calls/day * model unit price = estimated monthly). Provide sample small-medium-large scenarios and a single sentence about batching/cache levers.

Slide 6: Demo script: 90s warmup with sample prompt -> show token trace -> flip cache on -> show latency reduction -> simulate fallback to verify behavior. Include 'do not demo' list (live creds, PII).
Slide 7: Escalation ladder: SE -> Solutions Eng (ops) -> SRE on-call. Include Slack channel names, expected ack times (15/30/60). Link to the canonical runbook in GH.

Slide 8: Convert signals: sustained 7-day latency within target, cost per active user below threshold, ingestion stable, customer requests to increase quota or reserve capacity. Provide checklist for handoff to AE/CS.
practical_snippets: cURL repro: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"model":"rwdt-ephemeral","prompt":"hello"}'
Switch variant: set model param to rwdt-ephemeral-quant or rwdt-latency-slim
Token accounting: capture prompt_tokens + completion_tokens from response and multiply by unit price in console
fallback_policy_example: Trigger: 95th latency > 2x SLO for 5 minutes —> Action: route to same-region quantized variant for new requests (no cache warm)
Trigger: error rate > 1% for 3 minutes —> Action: enable edge cache hit policy for recent prefixes and notify ops
Trigger: sudden cost spike > 200% baseline in hourly window —> Action: throttle to per-route QPS cap and send rate-limit header to client
call_to_action: Share with SEs before next pilot kickoff. Ask SEs to run through the 15-min triage live once, add missing play triggers, and flag any customer-specific opt-outs. Target: integrate final checklist into pilot kickoff template by end of Q1.
